Pin all third-party GitHub Actions to a full commit SHA, not a tag
No untrusted GitHub-context (event/head_ref) interpolated into run: shell steps
Scope CI secrets to protected-branch environments only
Short-lived JWT access tokens
JWT algorithm explicitly hardcoded server-side — never trust the alg header
Opaque rotating refresh tokens stored server-side (not JWT)
Each refresh issues a new token and revokes the previous one
Theft detection — replaying a revoked token invalidates the token family
Server-side revocation on logout and password change
Session identifier regenerated on login before writing authenticated-user data (session fixation, CWE-384)
Frontend silent refresh on 401; hard logout on repeated failure
Access tokens in memory or HttpOnly cookies, not localStorage
Authentication decided server-side — no client-side password compare or predictable localStorage auth flag
JWT aud/iss/exp claims validated at decode (not just algorithm pinned)
All API endpoints require authentication (audit every route)
IDOR prevention — all resource queries filtered by authenticated user ID
WebSocket connections authenticated (token validation + ownership check)
Tenant isolation — every database row scoped to user_id
Structured security event logging on login failures and token theft
Authorization enforced — endpoints verify the caller has the required role/permission, not just authentication (BOLA/BFLA)
Business-rule constraints (booking windows, quotas, eligibility checks) enforced server-side, not only in frontend UI logic
Per-user rate limiting (falls back to IP for anonymous requests)
Rate limit backend persisted (Redis) — consistent across workers
Stricter limits on expensive or sensitive endpoints (auth, LLM routes)
Login — run bcrypt against a dummy hash when the user is not found (timing oracle)
Register — same response whether the email exists or not
File upload streaming size cap (memory-DoS protection)
SSRF guard on all URL-accepting endpoints (block RFC1918, link-local, metadata)
XXE-safe XML parsing (defusedxml or equivalent)
User-supplied content sanitized before injection into LLM prompts (incl. ChatML/Llama control tokens and system-role f-string injection — EXT-2B/EXT-5)
LLM input size capped to prevent token flooding / cost attacks
Content-Type / magic bytes validation on upload
Uploaded files saved under a server-generated name, never the client-supplied filename (prevents path traversal + dangerous-type write)
Path traversal on file serving — resolve and assert within base directory
Path() constructor never called with dynamic (user-controlled) argument — resolve and assert within base directory
Open redirect prevented — redirect targets vetted against an allow-list, not user input
SSRF guard on all server-side URL fetches, not only LLM paths (block RFC1918/link-local/metadata)
SSRF guard on JS/Node server-side HTTP client calls (fetch/axios/http/https)
Mass-assignment / over-posting prevented — request bodies not bound directly onto DB models
External user input wrapped in delimiters (XML/JSON tags) before prompts
LLM output sanitized before returning to client
SQL injection prevented via ORM parameterized queries (no raw SQL)
Supabase/PostgREST filter queries built via parameterized methods (no raw filter-string concatenation)
Go text/template not used where html/template's auto-escaping is needed for HTTP output
OS command injection prevented — no shell sink built from untrusted input
No code injection via a bare eval()/exec() sink fed dynamic content (independent of any LLM involvement)
No dynamic module import (importlib.import_module()/__import__()) with an attacker-influenceable, non-literal module name
No unsafe deserialization (pickle/yaml/torch.load/trust_remote_code) of untrusted data
No server-side template injection — user input never rendered as a template
No PHP local/remote file inclusion (LFI/RFI) via tainted include/require or dangerous stream wrappers
No reflected XSS via unescaped superglobal output (echo/print/short-echo-tag)
Scan repo text + user-uploaded files for invisible Unicode-tag characters and zero-width obfuscation chars (Glassworm / EXT-2A)
Scan source for homoglyph / mixed-script confusable identifiers (Cyrillic/Greek Latin-lookalikes — repo poisoning)
Post-retrieval chunk filter — scan RAG chunks for instruction-like patterns
No preg_replace() with the deprecated /e (eval) modifier
No extract() called directly on request superglobals — arbitrary variable overwrite
LLM output not auto-rendered with external images/links (markdown image data exfiltration)
Secondary LLM evaluates LLM output for suspicious content before delivery
Excel formula injection — safe_cell prefix on =, +, -, @ before openpyxl writes
CSV injection — same prefix rule on any CSV export
Lethal-trifecta assessment — private data + external comms + untrusted content inventoried with mitigations
LLM has no direct access to environment variables or secrets
RAG retrieval scoped to the authenticated user's data only
RAG pipeline has retrieval isolation controls — tenant filter, similarity threshold, and post-retrieval content filter
LLM output sanitized before reaching the client
LLM output never executed as code/command (no exec/eval/os.system/subprocess on model output)
Input size cap in place on all LLM-backed endpoints
Human-in-the-loop by design — users review and act on AI output
Audit LangChain chain types — disable/sandbox chains calling eval() or shell
Sanitize retrieved RAG chunks — chunk content is untrusted data, not instructions
Post-retrieval instruction filter — reject chunks with injection patterns
System prompt leakage protection — output filter blocks verbatim prompt fragments
System prompt not written to application logs at INFO or DEBUG level
System prompt not exposed in API error responses or exception detail fields
System prompt loaded from external config or env, not hardcoded as a source-code literal
LLM extraction confidence floor — flag low-confidence extracted values
LLM output truncation — cap extractor output tokens before the LLM call
Ingest-time provenance — log source, uploader, timestamp per vector-store document
Egress allowlisting — container only reaches required external APIs (deploy-time)
Scan ingested documents for invisible Unicode characters (Glassworm)
Per-user LLM cost / token budget cap with 429 on quota exceeded
LLM-as-Judge for RAG response evaluation (post-launch)
Per-agent tool allowlist — least privilege; an agent only gets the tools it needs
No tool-chaining exfiltration path — an agent is not given both a sensitive-read tool and an unrestricted external-send tool that combine into an exfil channel neither exposes alone
LLM tool executors return a fixed generic error, not a raw stringified exception or traceback — so provider/DB/internal error text is not leaked into the model's tool-result context
Human confirmation (or hard allowlist) required before high-impact agent actions (shell, delete, send, pay)
External triggers (inbound email/webhook) that resume an agent session with an elevated permission mode verify the sender before acting
Model-generated code executed only in an ephemeral, network-isolated sandbox (RCE prevention)
Tool/MCP connector descriptions treated as untrusted; no auto-load of third-party connectors; consent before external calls; mcp-remote pinned to >=0.1.16 (CVE-2025-6514)
MCP server's own HTTP/SSE/Streamable-HTTP transport requires authentication before accepting tool calls (not just client-side trust of servers it connects to)
MCP server's StreamableHTTP transport validates the Host header (DNS-rebinding protection), not just the bind address
MCP server's OAuth integration requests the smallest scope needed, and authorization/redirect URLs use a real HTTPS endpoint (not javascript:/file:/data:)
ML model downloads use HTTPS, hash verification, and Hub revision pins — no rug-pull or MITM substitution
No binary ML model artifact (.pkl/.pt/.h5/.gguf/.onnx/...) committed directly to source control
Committed pickle-family model file (.pkl/.pt/.pth/.bin/.joblib/.dill) opcode stream free of dangerous GLOBAL/STACK_GLOBAL imports
Committed Keras model file (.keras/.h5/.hdf5) free of Lambda-layer / marshalled-code-object RCE vectors
Committed GGUF model chat template free of Jinja sandbox-escape constructs
Committed ONNX model free of external-data path escapes and undisclosed custom operators
Lockfile committed and used in CI — no floating versions
Lockfile matches manifest — no dependency declared in package.json missing from package-lock.json's resolved set
Python CVEs patched — pip-audit clean on HIGH/CRITICAL
Frontend CVEs patched — npm audit clean on HIGH/CRITICAL
Full git history scanned for committed secrets — clean
API fuzz testing run against all endpoints — no new bugs
Remaining low/medium CVEs tracked with expiring waivers
Repo supply-chain health score (OpenSSF Scorecard)
Docker base image OS CVEs — rebuild with fresh patches at first deploy
Pin Docker base image to a specific digest (not just a tag)
Enable automated CVE notifications (Dependabot or equivalent)
Pinned dependencies meet the patched-version floor for known high-severity CVEs affecting the stack
Security headers on all responses (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, ...)
CORS restricted to explicit origins, methods, headers (no wildcard)
API docs (/docs, /redoc, /openapi.json) disabled in production
DEBUG defaults to False (fail-safe)
Server version header stripped
Cookies set with HttpOnly + Secure (+ SameSite) — session cookies not JS-readable / not sent in the clear
Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes on CDN-loaded scripts/stylesheets
Audit React components for dangerouslySetInnerHTML (LLM content = XSS vector)
Error responses do not leak stack traces, paths, or versions in production
Disable TLS 1.0/1.1 — only TLS 1.2 and 1.3
Restrict cipher suites — eliminate RC4, 3DES, CBC-mode
Verify with testssl.sh or nmap ssl-enum-ciphers before launch
Application runs as non-root user inside container
Dockerfile linted against CIS benchmark (Hadolint)
Container image scanned for CVEs (Trivy)
Base image OS CVEs — rebuild at deploy time
Docker network segmentation — DB reachable only from the API container
PostgreSQL NOT bound to 0.0.0.0 on the host
Read-only container filesystem (only required volumes writable)
Drop unnecessary Linux capabilities (--cap-drop ALL)
No world-open ingress in IaC — security-group ingress not opened to 0.0.0.0/0
Docker-compose does not writably bind-mount a root-equivalent host path
Docker-compose service sets no-new-privileges:true in security_opt
Docker-compose service sets a non-root user: directive
Docker-compose service sets read_only: true (immutable container root filesystem)
Compose services are segmented onto explicit networks, not the flat default network
Docker-compose does not bind-mount a sensitive host path (/sys, /dev, /home, credential dirs)
No credential-shaped docker-compose environment key holds a literal value
No docker-compose environment value embeds an inline connection-string credential
Every docker-compose service bounds memory and CPU
No docker-compose tmpfs mount re-enables exec/suid/dev
No docker-compose volume uses shared mount propagation
No docker-compose service explicitly disables its logging driver
RDS instance/cluster-instance not directly reachable from the internet (publicly_accessible not true)
S3 bucket Block Public Access controls (block_public_acls/block_public_policy/ignore_public_acls/restrict_public_buckets) not explicitly disabled
Azure Storage Account allows public blob access (allow_blob_public_access not explicitly false)
Azure Storage Account enforces HTTPS-only traffic (enable_https_traffic_only / https_traffic_only_enabled)
Azure API Management backend uses HTTPS and has authentication (credentials) configured
ARM template Azure App Service (Web/API/Function App) does not enforce HTTPS-only traffic
S3 bucket policy / KMS key policy does not grant an action to Principal: "*" without a narrowing Condition
S3 bucket AccessControl is not set to a public canned ACL (PublicRead/PublicReadWrite)
WAF WebACL DefaultAction is not ALLOW
Firewall — inbound on 22, 80, 443 only (UFW + cloud, both layers)
SSH key-only authentication (password + root login disabled)
Brute force protection on SSH and application (fail2ban)
SSH access restricted to an AllowUsers/AllowGroups account allowlist
Automatic OS security updates enabled
Egress allowlist — outbound restricted to required services
Every container routes DNS through the egress-allowlist resolver (no service bypasses it)
Linux audit score >= 80 (Lynis or equivalent)
Docker daemon passes CIS Docker Benchmark (Docker Bench Security)
Passwords hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12 or equivalent)
Refresh tokens stored as hashed values (not plaintext)
Non-cryptographic hash usage flagged (usedforsecurity=False)
All data scoped per user — RLS on every API-exposed table; no cross-user access
SECURITY DEFINER functions not EXECUTE-able by anon/authenticated
Supabase Vault material (decrypted views, vault-reading SECURITY DEFINER functions, the vault schema) not reachable by anon/authenticated; no literal secrets in SQL
SECURITY DEFINER functions do not EXECUTE arbitrary/dynamic SQL from arguments (RLS-bypass primitive)
Supabase service_role key never client-side — anon key + RLS is the client boundary
App DB role least privilege — no CREATEDB/CREATEROLE/superuser
pg_hba.conf audited — no trust auth for non-local connections
App connects to PostgreSQL over SSL (sslmode=require)
Database not exposed on host network (port not bound to 0.0.0.0)
Database encryption at rest enabled
Backups encrypted, stored off-server, restore tested periodically
PII minimization — audit stored user data; confirm all necessary
Artifact/memory/KV stores scoped per user — user data never written as shared/public (artifact-layer RLS)
Background tasks have explicit error handling (no silent drops)
Sensitive data not logged — request bodies, file content, financial figures
No weak / broken cryptography — no MD5/SHA-1 for security, no ECB mode, no `random` for secrets
No hardcoded password used as a function's default argument value (silently applies when the caller omits the argument)
Minimum password length policy is not hardcoded below 8 characters
Paramiko SSH client does not implicitly trust unknown host keys (no AutoAddPolicy/WarningPolicy) — verified against a known-hosts list
os.chmod()/lchmod()/fchmod() does not grant write or execute access to group/other permission bits
No PEM private key material of any label (incl. PKCS#8 encrypted) committed in source
No file existence/stat check followed by a separate use of the same path (time-of-check-to-time-of-use race, CWE-367)
No hardcoded LLM provider API key literal (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google AI/Hugging Face/Pinecone/Replicate/Groq/LangSmith/Supabase PAT) in Python source
AWS::CloudFormation::Authentication resource does not carry a literal password
Stripe webhook signature verified via construct_event on every event
Raw request body used for webhook verification (request.body(), not .json())
Stripe secret key never client-side — only the publishable key in the browser
Subscription state set only from verified Stripe events — never client params
Structured JSON logging on all requests (request ID, timestamp, status)
Security event logging — login failures, token theft, auth anomalies
Logs shipped to persistent external store (container logs are ephemeral)
Alerting on repeated login failures from same IP
Alerting on token theft detection events
Alerting on LLM quota exceeded events (cost monitoring)
Log retention policy defined (duration + storage location)
Sensitive data not present in logs — bodies, financial data, API keys
Auth regression tests — rotation, revocation, theft detection
Protected route tests — 401/403 with no/invalid token on every endpoint
Browser-level security checks (Playwright) — XSS, auth redirect, open redirect
DAST scan against live backend in CI
Prompt injection test suite against all LLM-backed endpoints
Excel export test — formula-prefixed cell values sanitized before writing
Stripe webhook test — fake events without valid signature rejected (401)
Re-run DAST locally against staging before first production deploy
Run testssl.sh against production TLS before launch
SECRET_KEY generated with a cryptographically secure method (32+ bytes)
Database password is a strong randomly generated value
All third-party API keys set in production environment (not placeholders)
ENVIRONMENT=production set
DEBUG=false set
DATABASE_ECHO=false set
ALLOWED_ORIGINS set to actual production domain (not localhost)
Stripe webhook secret configured
Rotate any API keys used during development
SSL certificate provisioned and auto-renewing
HTTP to HTTPS redirect configured
TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled; cipher suites hardened
Verified with testssl.sh — no CRITICAL cipher findings
Egress allowlist in place (only required external APIs reachable)
Firewall rules applied at OS and cloud provider level
App DB role confirmed least-privilege (no superuser, no DDL)
pg_hba.conf reviewed — no trust entries for non-local connections
PostgreSQL connecting over SSL (sslmode=require)
PostgreSQL port not exposed on host network
Backups configured, encrypted, tested with a restore
Docker image rebuilt from scratch (fresh OS patches)
Trivy scan on freshly built image — no CRITICAL/HIGH before deploy
Image pinned to specific digest in production compose file
Docker networks segmented — DB only reachable from API container
All GitHub Actions pinned to full commit SHA
VPS hardening audit passing (Lynis >= 80)
Verify /docs returns 404 in production
Smoke test full auth flow (register, login, refresh, logout)
Smoke test Stripe webhook with a test event
Verify rate limiting fires under repeated requests
Verify security headers present on all responses
Verify Excel export — formula-prefixed values escaped
Every PR: secret scan + SAST + dependency CVEs + container scan + DAST
Weekly scheduled CI run — new CVEs against existing locked dependencies
Monthly: review CVE alerts; rotate keys on team changes; review LLM cost per user
Quarterly: VPS hardening audit; DAST + fuzzer on staging; Lynis; testssl.sh
On incident: full re-audit + rotate all secrets immediately
AI asset inventory + model cards — models, datasets, tools, and connectors documented (NIST Map)
Input/output guardrail layer present (e.g. Llama Guard / NeMo Guardrails) — not system-prompt-only defense
Continuous eval / red-team gate in CI (prompt-injection + jailbreak suite runs on every change) (NIST Measure)
AI-specific incident-response runbook — prompt-injection / data-leak / model-abuse playbook with owners (NIST Manage)
Documented human-oversight + accountability for high-impact agent actions (who approves, who is responsible) (NIST Govern)
Users are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious from context (EU AI Act Art. 50(1), in force 2026-08-02)
IAM / cloud roles least-privilege — no Action:* or Resource:* under Allow
IAM policy statement least-privilege — no service-wide Action wildcard (e.g. iam:*, s3:*) under Allow
IAM policy statement scopes Resource to a specific ARN for actions that support resource-level permissions, instead of Resource: "*"
Privilege-escalation-class IAM actions (PassRole, AttachRolePolicy, sts:AssumeRole, ...) are granted only with a scoping Condition
IAM policy statement does not combine Effect: "Allow" with NotAction
Cognito User Pool has MFA enabled (ON or OPTIONAL, not OFF)
Cognito Identity Pool does not allow unauthenticated identities
No credential literal (password/secret/access_key/secret_key) hardcoded on a Terraform resource or provider attribute
Bicep resource adminUsername is a hardcoded string literal, not a parameter reference
Bicep param name looks like a secret but is not marked @secure()
Bicep @secure() parameter given a hardcoded, non-empty literal default value
Bicep output has a secret-shaped name but no @secure() decorator
Bicep CustomScript commandToExecute carries a secret under plaintext settings, not protectedSettings
Bicep nested deployment (outer-scoped) references a secure parameter or list*() function, leaking it into cleartext deployment history
Bicep .bicepparam file assigns a secret-shaped parameter a hardcoded literal value
No catastrophic-backtracking regex (ReDoS) on request-handling paths
FastAPI request models set extra=forbid (mass-assignment / over-posting prevention)
NoSQL operator injection prevented — no Mongo $-operator built from user input
CSRF protection on cookie-authenticated state-changing endpoints (CSRF token or SameSite=Strict/Lax) — not required for pure Authorization-header token auth
Slopsquatting defense — all dependencies pinned and verified against a trusted index before install; no unpinned/typo packages introduced by AI-suggested or auto-generated code
Autonomous agent loops have a hard iteration/recursion/tool-call cap, timeout, and circuit-breaker — chained actions cannot cascade or amplify without a hard stop

Persistent agent memory is write-validated and session/user-isolated — untrusted/agent output cannot be stored as durable memory that steers future decisions (memory poisoning / self-replicating injection)
Persistent agent memory carries a retention TTL — a poisoned or stale memory entry cannot persist indefinitely and re-contaminate future sessions
PII sent to an LLM and the response returned to the client has a redaction/anonymization layer (Anonymize before send, unmask only for the authorized caller)
LLM response text parsed as JSON is validated against a Pydantic schema before its fields are used in a decision
Excessive data exposure prevented — responses return only properties the caller is authorized to see; objects not serialized whole (no returning full ORM models with internal/other-user fields)
API inventory current — no deprecated, debug, or non-production (beta/v0/test) endpoints reachable in production
Data received from third-party/upstream APIs validated and sanitized before use — upstream responses treated as untrusted input (schema-validated, not passed to dangerous sinks)
Agent actions carry the end-user's identity and scope — tools/APIs invoked on a user's behalf must not use a shared high-privilege service identity (no confused-deputy)
Every agent tool call and high-impact action logged with inputs, identity, and outcome to a tamper-evident audit trail (detect rogue/misaligned behavior)
LangChain-core >= 0.3.81 / 1.2.5 in use; LLM-generated outputs not passed to langchain-core dumps/loads; secrets_from_env disabled (CVE-2025-68664 LangGrinch, CVSS 9.3)
LLM call result never used directly as a file path (MEDUSA-OUTPUT-PATH-001) — model output is attacker-controllable via prompt injection
User input never flows into LangChain load_prompt() or load_prompt_from_config() — legacy prompt-loading APIs allow arbitrary file read via path traversal (CVE-2026-34070)

MCP/tool connector schemas scanned for embedded instruction payloads; mutating tools annotated with destructiveHint — adversarial tool descriptions achieve 79%+ tool-call compliance even where text refusals succeed

MCP server config files free of hardcoded secrets, wildcard path grants, cleartext HTTP transport, parameter-name injection, unrestricted BCC-capable email tools, dangerous exec-target command fields, process-hijacking env vars, and interpreter launchers with inline-code-execution flags (MCP001-013, MCP018)
MCP server / agent-tool subprocess spawned with a scoped environment, not the full parent env (API keys, DB URLs, tokens) forwarded
MCP server does not resolve ${VAR}/$VAR placeholders in user-supplied config (e.g. a server URL) against its own process environment
MCP tool-handler URL-shaped parameters and MCP-config destinations (server_url/webhook_url/etc.) validated against a host/scheme allow-list before an outbound fetch
MCP sampling capability (server-initiated LLM completion requests) gated by a consent/elicitation flow, not wired up unconditionally
MCP tool catalogue built from an upstream tools/list response is bounded (count and per-item schema size), not accumulated without limit
MCP SEP-2243 Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name routable header cross-checked against the JSON-RPC body method before use in a routing or authorization decision
MCP tool gate (allowlist/read-only/non-destructive) enforced in the tools/call execution handler, not only in the tools/list discovery handler
MCP stdio server manifest fetched from a marketplace/registry not spawned directly (StdioServerParameters/StdioClientTransport) in the same function that fetched it
RAG knowledge base has adversarial-document integrity gate at ingest — scan chunk text for instruction-like content before indexing (5 crafted docs among millions achieve 90%+ attack success)
JWT key-source headers (jku/x5u/jwk) validated against an allowlist — never fetch verification keys from a token-supplied URL/key (ASVS 9.1.3)
Archive extraction guarded — cap uncompressed size + file count, and reject member paths escaping the target dir (zip-bomb / zip-slip) (ASVS 5.2.3/5.3.3)
Session tokens / API keys never accepted or placed in the URL or query string — only in body or header fields (avoids leakage to logs/Referer) (ASVS 14.2.1)
CSP defines object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none', and frame embedding controlled via frame-ancestors (not only the obsolete X-Frame-Options) (ASVS 3.4.3/3.4.6)
Authenticated/sensitive responses set Cache-Control: no-store so browsers and shared proxies do not cache private data (ASVS 14.3.2)
Source-control metadata (.git/.svn) excluded from build artifacts and not web-served in production (.dockerignore / no repo-root static mount) (ASVS 13.4.1)
Untrusted input encoded/escaped before being written to logs — no raw user data interpolated into log lines (CRLF log forging) (ASVS 16.4.1)
Client-supplied X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP not trusted for security decisions (rate limiting, IP allowlists) unless set by a trusted proxy (ASVS 4.1.3/15.3.4)
Security decisions fail closed — an exception in an auth/permission/validation path denies access, never defaults to allow (no fail-open / bare-except on a security check) (OWASP 2025 A10)
No DOM-based XSS sinks fed dynamic data (innerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval/new Function, setTimeout(str), location/href assignment from user/URL input)
HTML tags are not stripped via a hand-rolled wildcard regex (re.sub with <.*?> / <[^>]+>) instead of a real sanitizer
WebSocket handshake validates Origin against an allowlist (cross-site WebSocket hijacking) - distinct from token auth + ownership
No secrets in Dockerfile ARG/ENV (credentials as build args bake into image layers); use BuildKit --mount=type=secret

Auth dependency actually applied - a defined get_current_user/Security() dep is attached (route Depends or router/app dependencies) to every state-changing route; none left unauthenticated because the dep was never wired
Routes returning ORM/DB objects declare response_model (or explicit DTO) - no path op returns a raw SQLAlchemy instance without an output schema (FastAPI serializes the whole model)
TrustedHostMiddleware configured with a host allowlist - Host header validated (cache poisoning, poisoned reset links, internal-vhost SSRF)
Express/Node: outgoing email links (reset/invite/verification) are built from a trusted base URL, not the request's Host header
StaticFiles mounts a dedicated public asset dir, not repo root / app source / '/' - no StaticFiles(directory dot/slash/source tree) exposing .env/.py/.git
async def path operations do no blocking I/O - no sync DB driver/requests/time.sleep/blocking file read in an async route (event-loop stall = single-request DoS)
No unawaited async function call used as a truthy conditional (if/while) — Promise objects are always truthy
SQLAlchemy text()/raw execute() uses bound parameters, never f-string/percent/concat of request data (SQLi) - dep-free guard, not reliant on optional Semgrep
Inbound request models not instantiated via model_construct()/construct() - request data always goes through full Pydantic validation
SSRF blocklists normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (::ffff:x.x.x.x) before blocking — raw IPv4 blocklists bypassed via mapped-form cloud-metadata addresses
Hostname/URL allowlist regex has no unescaped dot before a domain suffix and ends with a `$` anchor (unanchored/unescaped-dot bypass)
URL scheme blocklist check covers javascript: as well as vbscript: and data: (not javascript: alone)
Raw URL substring never checked against a trusted domain instead of a parsed hostname (SSRF/open-redirect bypass)
Regex character class ranges (A-z, 0-Z, 0-z) do not admit unintended ASCII punctuation
indexOf()/lastIndexOf() used to emulate endsWith() correctly handle the -1 case (or endsWith() is used directly)
No javascript:/data: URL scheme in href/src bound from a variable (React does not sanitize URL attributes)
target=_blank anchors include rel=noopener noreferrer (reverse tabnabbing)
Vite production build does not ship source maps (build.sourcemap off; no .map in deploy)
No secret in VITE_-prefixed / import.meta.env vars - anything VITE_* is inlined into the client bundle
No provider API-key / secret literal (sk-proj-/AKIA/ghp_/AIza/pcsk_/r8_/gsk_/lsv2_/sbp_/...) hardcoded in client-side JavaScript
npm install/lifecycle scripts blocked by default (ignore-scripts / npm v12 allowlist) - postinstall supply-chain vector
pydantic-ai pinned to >= 1.99.0 — earlier versions carry SSRF in URL-download handling (CVE-2026-25580) with an incomplete fix bypassable via IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (CVE-2026-46678)
No unverified curl/wget output piped directly into a shell interpreter
window message listeners verify event.origin against an allowlist
No auth tokens written to localStorage/sessionStorage (static check - closes manual 2a-tokens-not-in-localstorage)
Starlette/FastAPI version >= 1.0.1 (BadHost patch) — malformed Host header cannot shift path/query boundaries to bypass route auth guards (CVE-2026-48710)
RLS enabled but no policy defined - accidental deny-all, or leak via stale grants
Permissive RLS policy USING (true) / WITH CHECK (true) - enabled-but-useless (authorizes everyone)
RLS enabled but not FORCE'd - the table owner role still bypasses every policy
Role granted BYPASSRLS - skips every RLS policy, cluster-wide
Default table privileges granted to PUBLIC - every future table exposed until RLS is remembered
RLS policy has an inverted auth check (auth function IS NULL OR ...) - anonymous callers hit a NULL short-circuit
RLS policy keys row visibility off current_user/session_user - no isolation over a pooled connection
RLS policy pins an identity column to a hardcoded literal, not a per-request value
Table has only RESTRICTIVE policies - silent deny-all
Function marked LEAKPROOF - a false promise leaks RLS-hidden row contents
Policy's current_setting() names an unqualified parameter - likely a dropped app-namespace prefix
RLS policy pattern-matches a column against an auth-context value - a wildcard session value bypasses it
Role can SET ROLE to a BYPASSRLS role - an RLS-bypass path invisible from its own attributes
